replies.text:
Direct from agent readout

"The main scenes:

TimeWhat happens
0–8s
A light sweeps across the gold wall and ripples run through the tiles
8–21s
The fish's tiles lift off and swim as a flock, leap, dive into the sea, and land back in place
~21–34s
Two cranes and a dove fly out of the wall the same way
34–40s
A wave flips every tile over to its night face: navy glass, silver stars and a crescent moon
40–58s
The stars peel off and swarm into a constellation
58s
A second wave flips the wall back to day
63–72s
The whole wall lets go into a spiral, then snaps back from the centre outward
75s
One last tile flips, then fade out and loop
The sound is all synthesized in the browser: a chord pad that swells during the spiral, a shimmer, and a small click whenever a tile lands.

Changes I made after watching it frame by frame:

Fish: its body was gold on a gold wall and read as a blob. It's now copper and orange glass with a blue outline.
Flock shape: the fish, crane and dove tiles are held more tightly and flutter less, so each figure keeps its shape in flight.
Reflections: the moving light was washing out the sun and moon, so its reflections are now tighter and less intense.
Plaster: the background stripes had too much contrast, so I toned them down.
Spiral: the inner tiles now rotate faster than the outer ones, so the spiral arms are visible.
Still rough:

The sky looks pale for about a second during the day-to-night flip, while the tiles are turned edge-on. It clears once they settle.
The night sea is close to black. It could use a little more teal."
